titel: The Origin of American Authoritarianism | Episode 6

einzeiler: How the blueprint for US colonialism shaped modern American authoritarianism and…
kurzfassung: The episode explores how the US Constitution and the Northwest Ordinance were written simultaneously as blueprints for democracy and colonialism. Legal scholars explain how colonial tactics used against Indigenous nations and territories are now applied domestically through the boomerang of empire. The discussion highlights historical Native resistance, including Cherokee diplomacy at the Constitutional Convention, and reflects on confronting this history.
stichpunkte: Ryan Eckln and other US citizens were detained by ICE agents in Minneapolis under questionable legal justifications.
The Articles of Confederation provided a weak federal government without an executive power before being rewritten in 1787.
The Northwest Ordinance established a top-down, non-representative colonial system for governing territories west of the Mississippi.
Founders attempted to build a constitutional republic and an empire simultaneously, creating dual blueprints for democracy and colonialism.
The boomerang of empire explains how authoritarian practices developed in colonial contexts are eventually brought home to govern domestic populations.
Representatives from Indigenous nations, including Cherokee delegate Scontoya, traveled to Philadelphia to demand respect for territorial treaties.
The supremacy clause of the US Constitution established federal statutes, the Constitution, and treaties as the supreme law of the land.
Host Rebecca Nagel reflects on visiting her ancestral home in Hiawassee, which was burned to the ground during the Revolutionary War.

beschreibung:
We’ve all been told our founders created a democracy. Rebecca talks with Maggie Blackhawk (Ojibwe) about why that's only half the story. Because our founders also wanted an empire. And so, they built both: a democracy that gave its citizens a voice and a vote; and an empire that controlled the lives and lands of people who had no say. That playbook never went away. Today, when our government wants to annex Greenland, deny citizenship to people born here, or put migrants in detention camps, it uses laws first passed to colonize Indigenous nations to do so.
